materiality.rule: A change is the account's middle impact figure under the later vintage minus the one under the earlier vintage. Both use the same book, window, cutoff, accounts and nodes. The change is in pesos. It is material when its size reaches the threshold by the comparator.
materiality.statement: The materiality line comes before any figure. Every call that writes a figure or classifies a change needs it. It is the first block of every record.
materiality.basis: This line is a policy of the method demonstration. The owner has not given a line. It is never a business limit.

selection.rule: The data build picks one vintage per region. It takes the newest vintage of that region issued at or before the cutoff. A region with none takes the newest system vintage.

heat.rule: Shade 0 holds no uncovered MWh. Shades 1 to 4 split the day's largest cell into four equal steps. A cell takes the first step whose edge reaches its value.

method.uncovered: Uncovered MWh for a node and hour is demand MW minus covering contract MW, times one hour. It is never below zero. An account's figure is the sum of its nodes.
method.cover: A contract covers a node and hour when it is on that node and lists that clock hour. The contract must be in term on the hour's own date. A fixed-price contract lists all 24 hours. A time-of-use block lists its own hours.
method.profile: The book holds one 24-hour demand profile per node. Each window hour reads the profile at its clock hour. A window of whole days repeats the profile once per day, as IMPACT-1 does. The book refuses a window that crosses a midnight inside a day.
method.cutoff: The book records the day a contract term starts, not the day of signing. The book refuses a cutoff before the term start of a contract in scope. It cannot say if anyone knew that contract then.

materiality.rule: A change is the account's middle impact figure under the later vintage minus the one under the earlier vintage. Both use the same book, window, cutoff, accounts and nodes. The change is in pesos. It is material when its size reaches the threshold by the comparator.
materiality.statement: The materiality line comes before any figure. Every call that writes a figure or classifies a change needs it. It is the first block of every record.
materiality.basis: This line is a policy of the method demonstration. The owner has not given a line. It is never a business limit.

vintage.band_width: the vintage states three levels per hour

window.clock: naive Asia/Manila local hours (UTC+8, no daylight saving), the price target contract's clock

as_of.rule: A vintage can price a question only when its issue time is at or before the question's cutoff. A date cutoff closes at the next Manila midnight.

method.impact: For one node, hour and band level, the impact equals uncovered MWh times (band level minus reference price). A node's figure is the sum over the window's hours. An account's figure is the sum over its nodes. The sign stays, so a negative figure is a gain.
method.reference: The reference price is the MW-weighted price of the contracts that cover the node and hour, in centavos. The uncovered volume is the unhedged part of the hour. The covering contracts state the price of the hedged part. No record holds a benchmark price. So the method refuses an hour with uncovered volume and no covering contract.
method.band: The band is the vintage's three levels at each window hour. The method reads them only when the outlook record is valid and its record id matches the named id. The SHA-256 of the values file must match the record too. A file with the middle value only gives a band of zero width.
method.sum: The three sums form a band, not a probability. A sum of hourly quantiles is the quantile of the sum only when the hours move together. IMPACT-1 sums them the same way.
method.uncovered: Uncovered MWh for a node and hour is demand MW minus covering contract MW, times one hour. It is never below zero. An account's figure is the sum of its nodes.
method.cover: A contract covers a node and hour when it is on that node and lists that clock hour. The contract must be in term on the hour's own date. A fixed-price contract lists all 24 hours. A time-of-use block lists its own hours.

materiality.rule: A change is the account's middle impact figure under the later vintage minus the one under the earlier vintage. Both use the same book, window, cutoff, accounts and nodes. The change is in pesos. It is material when its size reaches the threshold by the comparator.
materiality.statement: The materiality line comes before any figure. Every call that writes a figure or classifies a change needs it. It is the first block of every record.
materiality.basis: This line is a policy of the method demonstration. The owner has not given a line. It is never a business limit.

vintage.band_width: the vintage states three levels per hour

window.clock: naive Asia/Manila local hours (UTC+8, no daylight saving), the price target contract's clock

as_of.rule: A vintage can price a question only when its issue time is at or before the question's cutoff. A date cutoff closes at the next Manila midnight.

method.impact: For one node, hour and band level, the impact equals uncovered MWh times (band level minus reference price). A node's figure is the sum over the window's hours. An account's figure is the sum over its nodes. The sign stays, so a negative figure is a gain.
method.reference: The reference price is the MW-weighted price of the contracts that cover the node and hour, in centavos. The uncovered volume is the unhedged part of the hour. The covering contracts state the price of the hedged part. No record holds a benchmark price. So the method refuses an hour with uncovered volume and no covering contract.
method.band: The band is the vintage's three levels at each window hour. The method reads them only when the outlook record is valid and its record id matches the named id. The SHA-256 of the values file must match the record too. A file with the middle value only gives a band of zero width.
method.sum: The three sums form a band, not a probability. A sum of hourly quantiles is the quantile of the sum only when the hours move together. IMPACT-1 sums them the same way.
method.uncovered: Uncovered MWh for a node and hour is demand MW minus covering contract MW, times one hour. It is never below zero. An account's figure is the sum of its nodes.
method.cover: A contract covers a node and hour when it is on that node and lists that clock hour. The contract must be in term on the hour's own date. A fixed-price contract lists all 24 hours. A time-of-use block lists its own hours.

as_of.rule: A vintage can price a question only when its issue time is at or before the question's cutoff. A date cutoff closes at the next Manila midnight.

method.impact: For one node, hour and band level, the impact equals uncovered MWh times (band level minus reference price). A node's figure is the sum over the window's hours. An account's figure is the sum over its nodes. The sign stays, so a negative figure is a gain.
method.reference: The reference price is the MW-weighted price of the contracts that cover the node and hour, in centavos. The uncovered volume is the unhedged part of the hour. The covering contracts state the price of the hedged part. No record holds a benchmark price. So the method refuses an hour with uncovered volume and no covering contract.
method.band: The band is the vintage's three levels at each window hour. The method reads them only when the outlook record is valid and its record id matches the named id. The SHA-256 of the values file must match the record too. A file with the middle value only gives a band of zero width.
method.sum: The three sums form a band, not a probability. A sum of hourly quantiles is the quantile of the sum only when the hours move together. IMPACT-1 sums them the same way.
method.uncovered: Uncovered MWh for a node and hour is demand MW minus covering contract MW, times one hour. It is never below zero. An account's figure is the sum of its nodes.
method.cover: A contract covers a node and hour when it is on that node and lists that clock hour. The contract must be in term on the hour's own date. A fixed-price contract lists all 24 hours. A time-of-use block lists its own hours.
